title: Semiconductor Absolute Maximum Ratings
author: P
text:
T

TomCee
New member

All:

Certainly with improved processing and manufacturing, certain processes impact perfomance specifications-in particular for analog integrated circuits.

Part number specifications generally define the performance parameters and Absolute Maximum Ratings.

If Process Progression results in the Absolute Maximum Operating Voltage of a particular part being reduced, shouldn't this demand a new part number?

Of course many part families may have a 5V and 3.3V etc versions, but these have unique part numbers to define this critical parameter.

I am referring to the recent reduction of Absolute Maxinmum Operating Voltage of the NE5532 Dual Operational Amplifier.

This part, developed by Signetics around 1979 and well accepted due to its low noise and high Absolute Maximun Operating Voltage of 44VDC. It has been a mainstay in professional audio since then - in many cases operating at 40 to 42 VDC (reference Otari, Audio Designs and others).

Recently, a major manufacturer (one of several suppliers) of this part has reduced the Maximum Operating Voltage to 36VDC.

New processes of course result in the lower voltage.
Further, there are higher performance parts and this part would not necessarily be implemented in new designs.

HOWEVER, as these parts will still be in the market for some time, the part number should reflect this decrease in Operating Voltage; many Purchasing Agents do not read the spec sheets - they use only the commercial part number.

If this reduced AbsMax part is installed in a existing design, likely failure and other undesirable results could occur.

Regards,
TomC
